per_pair.why: B groups health, dash meter, currency, room-progress track and ability slots into framed, consistent dark panels hugging the corners, while A scatters unframed counters, ammo icons and a leftover '60 FPS' debug readout over the playfield.

B's 'ARENA CLEARED' sits on a gold-ruled dark ribbon with a crisp drop-shadowed display font, whereas A's clear message is five lines of raw stacked green text with no panel, colliding with the HUD and the scene.
A's hit reads instantly through a sustained full-screen red wash and a big numeric bar visibly dropping 6/8 to 3/8, while B's thin red frame flash and tiny heart pips are easy to miss at a glance.

At the small size B's corner panels and icon slots stay tidy and clear of the action, while A's dense left column of bar, icons, ammo counts and weapon cards turns into soft clutter, even though its numbers are still bold.

loser_biggest_gap: Put the HUD into a framed, cohesive panel system: give the health/ammo/icon cluster (top-left), the gold/kill/area counters (top-right) and the weapon cards (bottom-left) dark, bordered backing plates with consistent padding and one shared type style, and remove the '60 FPS' debug readout.
loser_other_gaps: Replace the plain stacked green 'AREA CLEAR!' text with a designed banner: one short headline on a bordered ribbon or plate, animated in and out, with flavour copy cut or moved to a smaller secondary line.
Cut down the top-left column (ammo-type icons, reserve count, secondary weapon icons) so it can be read in one glance; show only the active resource prominently and dim or collapse the rest.
Add a room/level progress indicator and ability or cooldown slots with their own framing, so the run state reads as part of the HUD rather than a bare '3-3' / 'AREA 2' label.
Tone the hurt wash down to a short pulse plus an edge vignette so the playfield stays readable during multi-second damage, and keep the health-bar drop animated (white lag chunk) as the main signal.
reasoning: B's HUD looks like a finished product: every element sits on a consistent framed dark panel, icons share one pixel style, the corners are used neatly, and the clear banner is a designed ribbon rather than raw text. A's HUD is bold and functional, and its large numeric health bar plus full-screen red wash make damage more obvious than B's subtle red frame and small hearts. But A's elements are unframed, crowded into a tall left column, mix several type and icon treatments, and still show a debug FPS counter, which reads as prototype rather than polished indie. Overall B wins on finish, cohesion and keeping clear of the action, and A only wins on raw hurt feedback.
